text:
mike-infra: FYI — seeing a spike of GPU nodes in eu-west1 flip to NotReady / NoSchedule. Started around 2359999900. ~9/22 gpu nodes affected, a few pods pending.

alex-oncall: ack, thanks. any kubelet logs or device plugin traces?

mike-infra: quick paste from one node:
```
$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-17
Name: gpu-node-17
Conditions: Ready False
Events:
  Warning  FailedMount  device plugin handshake failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
  Warning  NodeNotReady  kubelet has no available CAs for CSR rotation, kubelet certificate rotation failed
```
Also seeing a bunch of CSR objects piling up pending approval from the controller. infra-monitor-bot alerted on CSR queue depth > 100.

tara-sre: interesting. we rotated cluster certs earlier today but that was supposed to be safe. could the csr controller be starved?

ingrid-eng: cluster-autoscaler is also not adding capacity because most of the gpu pools are tainted NoSchedule, CA thinks capacity OK but pods are unschedulable. we have pending burst for batch jobs.

alex-oncall: can we try a targeted restart of the nvidia device plugin ds on a single bad node first?

mike-infra: tried that on 2 nodes: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system` — pods come up but still fail handshake within seconds. kubelet logs show TLS handshake errors during plugin registration and then CSR creation spam.

tara-sre: possible race between kubelet cert rotation and device plugin using the socket. if kubelet rotated cert and old socket was invalid, plugin reconnect fails and kernel udev noise might occur.

alex-oncall: quick mitigation plan:
1) cordon a couple affected nodes to stop scheduling more work: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17`
2) drain non-daemonset pods: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
3) ssh and restart kubelet service on the node or reboot if kubelet unresponsive
4) after kubelet back, restart device-plugin ds and watch registration

mike-infra: doing cordon/drain on 3 nodes now. leaving one node uncordoned so CA can still see capacity.

infra-monitor-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-489, severity P2, impacted nodes: 9, region: eu-west1

ingrid-eng: long term we should increase CSR controller QPS and apiserver clientBurst for kube-controller-manager during rotations. Also consider small rollout window for cert rotation on GPU pools.

tara-sre: agreed. can we also add a readiness probe for nvidia-device-plugin that fails fast so CA knows nodes are not usable? right now device plugin failing silently and nodes appear Ready enough for CA decisions.

alex-oncall: note: cluster-autoscaler logs show scale up suppressed because node group has unready nodes but autoscaler considers desired capacity reached. we might need to temporarily lower the scaleDown/scaleUp thresholds.

mike-infra: quick log snippet from CA: `scale up skipped: nodes not suitable, pending pods: 34`

ingrid-eng: finance FYI: this incident may push some teams to manual on-demand instances to finish jobs, may spike cost by an estimated $3-5k if prolonged. tagging billing.

mike-infra: update: restarted kubelet on 4 nodes, device-plugin re-registered successfully on 3 of them. two nodes still failing with CSR errors.

tara-sre: for the two stubborn nodes can you capture `/var/log/syslog` and `/var/log/kubelet.log` and attach here? also output `kubectl get csr -o wide | head -n 30`.

mike-infra: attaching summaries in thread. captured high rate of CSR create attempts and apiserver returning 429s for controller requests. seemed like apiserver was briefly saturated during rotation.

alex-oncall: next steps: patch rollout to bump controller-manager clientBurst to 200 and controller QPS to 50 in a canary in eu-west1, then re-run cert rotation with smaller batch size.

mike-infra: implementing the patch to controller-manager on canary control plane. will circle back in 15m.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kube-system/controller-manager canary eu-west1 -> image tag cm-v1.2.3-canary at 2360000200

mike-infra: canary looked healthy, CSR queue dropped to normal and device-plugin re-registered across the rest of nodes. scaling resumed.

ingrid-eng: good catch. please put the controller-manager QPS/burst change into a postmortem action item and add a short runbook for gpu cert rotations.

tara-sre: adding runbook item: rotate certs in 10% increments for gpu pools, monitor CSR queue, pause if apiserver 429s spike.

mike-infra: incident is resolved for now. reopening if any regressions. closing notes: root cause was apiserver/controller-manager saturation during cert rotation causing kubelet CSR flow to fail and device-plugin registration to repeatedly break, leaving nodes effectively unschedulable.

alex-oncall: thanks everyone. filing incident postmortem and remedial PRs. :thumbsup:

mike-infra: closing when postmortem link is posted.
